content.title: Global Automation Atlas
content.abstract: Whether automation can replace or support workers depends not only on task content, but also on the conditions under which work is performed. Existing exposure measures typically assign fixed scores to tasks, capturing country differences only through employment structure. We use a large language model to classify 18,797 tasks in 124 economies by feasible exposure, labour substitution or augmentation, technology type and reliance on artificial intelligence. Accounting for country conditions changes occupation rankings and improves predictions of firms’ technology use. Exposure ranges from 3.3%
